content:
It gives the maintainers of the Sphere Packing Project great pleasure to announce a major milestone in the formalization effort: we now have a sorry-free Lean proof of the theorem that the optimal sphere packing in R8\mathbb{R}^8R8 is the E8E_8E8​ lattice packing. The formal proof largely follows Maryna Viazovska's original Fields-Medal-winning work from 2016, using modular forms and Fourier-analytic methods.

What makes this milestone particularly notable is the role played by Gauss, an autoformalization agent developed by Math Inc. Building on the project’s Lean code base and on the detailed blueprint developed by the maintainers and community collaborators, Gauss carried out all the remaining steps needed to produce a proof that has been fully checked by the Lean kernel.

The project team is already in the process of reviewing and revising Gauss' code, thereby ensuring that it meets the editorial standards of the formalization community. This process will ensure that the code is maintainable and reusable, and that it will support future formalization work. Gauss' remarkable contribution has saved the project months of effort, and Gauss will continue to play a role in the revisions.

We want to thank everyone who has contributed to the effort, human and AI contributors alike, for the many pieces of infrastructure, lemmas, refactors, reviews, and experiments that accumulated into a codebase strong enough for this final step. We’re excited to collaborate with Math Inc and the broader Lean community on the remaining engineering and consolidation work.

We include the following links for reference.

  • Main Sphere Packing repository: http://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/
  • Gauss code: see spherepacking#341

— The Sphere Packing Maintainers (@Chris Birkbeck, myself, @Seewoo Lee, @Bhavik Mehta, @Maryna Viazovska)

We would like to acknowledge the invaluable support of @Jeremy Avigad, @Kevin Buzzard, @Pietro Monticone, the Mathlib maintainers, and the Institute for Computer-Aided Reasoning in Mathematics.

We are honored to have assisted Sid and the rest of the team with completing the formalization of sphere packing in 8 dimensions. The latest version of our autoformalization agent, Gauss, was able to complete the proof relying solely on the blueprint from Sid’s repository, requiring no additional mathematical hints. This result would not have been possible without the phenomenal blueprint and foundations laid by Sid and the rest of the team. We also want to acknowledge the incredible work done by the broader Lean community on Mathlib. Formalizations of this scale will soon be commonplace and we believe it is important to ensure that the code can be upstreamed and made useful.

We look forward to continuing to work together to review the PR, improve the quality of the formalization, and push the boundaries of what AI and mathematicians can achieve together.
For questions and comments, see #Sphere packing in 8 dimensions > Discussion for Autoformalization.
